output.brief:
The evidence doesn't show that the three-person night rota caused the rise in falls, and it doesn't rule it out. Recorded falls roughly doubled, but three things muddy that figure. The two homes switched to the Tallyline app on 1 July. A check of Q2 handover notes found at least three unreported falls, and Q3 can't be checked the same way. Unwitnessed "found on floor" falls rose from 5 to 14. Per 1,000 bed days, both homes' Q3 rates (3.7) sit inside their historical ranges. Five earlier rises of 70% or more at single homes fell back without action. A real rise of around 40% would still take two to three quarters to show, so "nothing changed" isn't proven. Nobody has call-bell timings from before June. Ashby Fold's median answer time is 3 min 40 s, and Penmor Lodge's panel can't record answer times. Frailer admissions and GP medication changes are plausible but untested.

Recommendation: don't return to four staff now and don't halt the rollout. Keep the pilot under its pause criteria. Show falls as rates, with the reporting change marked. Start manual sampling of night call-bell response times at both homes. Review the rollout in late January with Q4 data. Don't issue capability warnings, and don't withdraw the app. Escalate sooner if harm falls or response times worsen.
